design_critique: 1) Speed margin is unsupported. The 3.0 s limit on a 4 to 5 m course needs an average of 1.5 to 1.67 m/s, so base_speed 1.5 is at or below the minimum, not above it. The rationale assumes base_speed maps linearly to ground speed, but the contract only says PWM = 4095*min(1, base_speed/2). Rolling resistance, drag, tyre slip, motor ramp-up, battery sag and slowing through the tighter bends all reduce the real average. Nothing in the inputs shows that 1.5 gives 1.5 m/s on average, so the likely failure is not finishing in time (completion 0, progress capped near 0.9). The draft should either raise base_speed toward 1.8 to 2.0 or justify the choice with a stated speed model. 2) Steady offset is not handled. The simulator has a fixed left/right motor mismatch. With ki 0, a P+D loop settles at a constant bias offset from the centre line, which raises rms_error and can push max_error toward the 0.06 m off-track limit on long runs. A small ki (for example 0.2 to 0.5) is bounded by the +/-2 integral clamp, so windup is limited. The rationale's windup argument does not address this. 3) Sensor look-ahead is short. Sensors sit at y 0.03 m ahead of the axle, about 20 ms of travel at 1.5 m/s. That gives little anticipation on bends. Moving the sensors forward (up to y 0.08) would add lead time, and this is the most likely lever for keeping the robot on the line at speed. 4) Off-track allowance is misread. The limit is max(0.06, tape_half_width + body_width/4) = max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.03) = 0.06 m for body_width 0.12. Body widths below 0.19 never change the limit, so body_width 0.12 does not widen the allowance as the rationale claims. 5) Signal is not proportional to offset. signal is a reading-weighted average, so its relation to offset is nonlinear and saturates at the weight extremes. The claim that signal is 'proportional to the line offset' is not supported. The 875 PWM per unit figure is correct arithmetic (2.5 x 350) but only applies to the signal, not to the offset. 6) Sensor coverage is overstated. Footprints are 12 mm wide on a 20 mm pitch, leaving 8 mm gaps. The tape is 25 mm wide, so at some offsets a single sensor may read partially, and 'always covered by one or two sensors' is not verified. 7) Derivative noise is not quantified. kd 0.2 on signal changes can amplify sensor noise into PWM jitter of order 100 counts or more. The draft does not estimate this. 8) Geometry claims are unquantified. 'Moderate turning radius' and 'reasonable speed-to-turn ratio' are asserted without calculation. Yaw inertia is 0.8*(0.18^2+0.12^2)/12, about 0.0037 kg m^2, which the draft never reports, so 'low inertia' has no baseline to compare against.
rationale_critique: The rationale asserts performance (rms_error under 0.03 m, few line-loss events) with no supporting calculation or prior race data, and presents contract reasoning as if it were measured. It mislabels several contract facts: the off-track allowance is not widened by body_width at this value, the sensor coverage claim is stronger than the geometry supports, and 'proportional' signal is not what the weighted-average formula gives. It also treats the speed target as having headroom when the 1.5 setting equals the minimum average required, which contradicts its own stated goal. The rationale does not state which failure mode it expects to see first beyond a general 'too fast or too slow' statement, so the race will not discriminate between hypotheses well. It gives no alternative designs or sensitivity ranges, so the revision has no basis for choosing between kp, kd, speed and sensor placement changes. Finally, it does not state what evidence would change its mind (for example, a completion time above 3 s would mean raising base_speed; repeated oscillation would mean lowering kp or raising kd).
